headline: Peruvian Sol Opens Near S/3.45 per Dollar Amid Copper Price Drop
summary: The Peruvian sol opened at S/3.450 per U.S. dollar, marking a slight decline alongside falling global copper prices and cautious sentiment across foreign exchange markets.
why: Peru is the world's second-largest copper exporter. Fluctuation in copper export revenues directly influences domestic currency valuation and trade balance figures.

impacts.name: US Dollar / Peruvian Sol
impacts.why: Falling international copper prices weighed on the Peruvian sol against the U.S. dollar.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Weakness in global metal commodity prices pressured the currency of major copper-producing nations.
